stem: Why does a computer need input devices?

options.content: To capture data and convert it into a digital form the computer can process
options.rationale: Correct: the CPU can only process digital (binary) data.

options.content: To show the results of processing to the user on a screen
options.rationale: That is the job of output devices.

options.content: To keep data safe when the computer is switched off
options.rationale: That is the job of secondary storage.

options.content: To carry out calculations on the data that has been entered
options.rationale: Calculations are done by the CPU (the ALU).

explanation: Input devices capture data from users or the environment and convert it into digital data for the CPU.

stem: Which input device uses a small camera to take many images of the surface it is moved across?

options.rationale: Correct: it compares successive images to work out movement.
A keyboard detects which key switch completes a circuit.
A microphone detects sound vibrations.
A 2D scanner copies flat documents placed on glass.

explanation: An optical mouse shines an LED on the surface and compares images taken hundreds of times a second.

stem: When a barcode is scanned, what happens to the light that falls on the **black** bars?

options.rationale: Correct: black bars absorb light; white spaces reflect it.

options.content: It is reflected back to the sensor
options.rationale: It is the white spaces that reflect the light.
The scanner detects light, not sound.

options.content: It passes straight through the label
options.rationale: The label is not transparent; the light is absorbed or reflected.

explanation: The sensor detects the pattern of reflected light (white) and no reflection (black), which is converted into the barcode number.

stem: How does a **capacitive** touch screen detect where it is touched?

options.content: Pressure pushes two flexible layers together and completes a circuit
options.rationale: That describes a resistive touch screen.

options.content: The finger breaks invisible beams of light crossing the screen
options.rationale: That describes an infra-red touch screen.

options.content: A finger changes the electrical charge at that point on the screen
options.rationale: Correct: the finger conducts electricity and disturbs the electrostatic field.

options.content: A camera behind the screen photographs the finger
options.rationale: Touch screens do not use a camera to locate the touch.

explanation: Capacitive: change in charge; resistive: layers pressed together; infra-red: beams broken.

stem: In a microphone, what converts the electrical signal from the diaphragm into data the computer can store?

options.rationale: A DAC does the opposite, for example to drive a speaker.
An actuator is an output device that causes movement.
Correct: the microphone's signal is analogue and must be digitised.
A barcode reader reads printed codes.

explanation: Sound → diaphragm vibrates → varying electrical signal (analogue) → ADC → digital data.

stem: A mine in Hwange wants a touch screen in its control room. Workers wear thick gloves and the screen must be very large. Which type is most suitable?

options.rationale: It needs a conductive touch, so it does not work with thick gloves.
Correct: it detects any object breaking the beams and suits very large screens.
It works with gloves but needs firm pressure and is easily damaged on a large display.

options.content: A screen with no touch input and a keyboard
options.rationale: The question asks for a touch screen.

explanation: Infra-red screens work with gloves or any object and scale well to large sizes.
hints: Which type works with any object touching it?

stem: A restaurant in Victoria Falls wants customers to open its online menu on their phones by pointing the camera at a printed code on each table. Which type of code should it print?

options.rationale: A barcode holds only a short number and needs a barcode scanner.
A magnetic stripe needs a card reader and cannot be printed on a table card.
A 3D model is created by a 3D scanner; it is not a code.
Correct: QR codes hold enough data for a web address and are read by phone cameras.

explanation: QR codes store more data than barcodes (such as a URL) and can be read at any angle by a phone camera and app.
hints: Which code can hold a website address and be read by a phone camera?

stem: A museum in Bulawayo wants to make an accurate digital model of a carved stone bird so that copies can be made on a 3D printer. Which input device is needed?

options.rationale: A 2D scanner only copies flat documents and photographs.
It reads barcodes, not shapes.
One photograph is a flat 2D image, not a 3D model.
Correct: it measures many points on the object's surface to build a 3D model.

explanation: A 3D scanner captures the shape of a solid object as a digital 3D model, which can be sent to a 3D printer.
hints: Which device captures the shape of a solid object?

stem: A resistive touch screen works when the user is wearing gloves.
explanation: True. A resistive screen responds to pressure, so any object, including a gloved finger, can press the layers together.

stem: A QR code can only be read when it is held exactly upright in front of the camera.
explanation: False. The three corner squares let the software work out the code's position and angle, so it can be read at any angle.

stem: Match each input device to how it works.

right.content: Light falls on a sensor made of millions of light-sensitive cells
A moving row of sensors captures light reflected from a page on glass
A key press completes a circuit in a grid of wires
A diaphragm vibrates and produces a varying electrical signal

explanation: Each device captures a different kind of data and converts it into digital form.

stem: Match each task to the most suitable input device.

left.content: Reading product codes at a supermarket till
Copying a printed school report into a computer

explanation: Choose the device that captures that kind of data quickly and accurately.
hints: Think about the data in each situation: text, sound, a product code, a shape.

stem: Complete the description of how a barcode scanner works.

payload.template: The scanner shines red light across the barcode. The white spaces {{blank:a}} the light and the black bars absorb it. A {{blank:b}} detects the reflected light, and the pattern is converted into a {{blank:c}} number. The computer uses this number to look up the product in a {{blank:d}}.

explanation: Light → white reflects, black absorbs → sensor → digital number → database look-up.

stem: A digital camera's image sensor is 4608 pixels wide and 3456 pixels high. How many light-sensitive pixels does the sensor have?
workedSolution:
1. Pixels = width × height.
2. 4608 × 3456 = 15925248 pixels, about 15.9 million.

stem: Name the software that converts a scanned image of printed text into text that can be edited in a word processor (full name or abbreviation).
explanation: Optical character recognition (OCR) turns the scanned image of text into editable characters.

stem: Describe how an optical mouse detects that it has been moved. [3]

points.description: An LED shines light onto the surface under the mouse
A light sensor / tiny camera takes many images of the surface every second
A processor compares successive images to work out the direction and distance moved, and sends this to the computer

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: An LED lights up the surface. A small camera takes hundreds of images a second, and the mouse's processor compares each image with the last to calculate the direction and distance of movement, which is sent to the computer.

hints: Start with the light, end with the movement sent to the computer.

stem: Explain how a **resistive** touch screen detects where it is touched. Give **one** drawback of this type of screen. [4]

points.description: Two (flexible) layers with conductive coatings separated by a small gap
Pressing pushes the top layer onto the bottom layer, completing a circuit
The point of contact is calculated from the change in voltage / current
Drawback: needs pressure / top layer easily scratched or damaged / less clear image / usually no multi-touch

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A resistive screen has two conductive layers separated by a tiny gap. Pressing the screen pushes the layers together and completes a circuit; the change in voltage tells the computer where it was touched. A drawback is that the soft top layer can be scratched easily.

explanation: Layers, pressure, circuit completed, location calculated.
hints: Describe the layers, then what happens when the screen is pressed.

stem: A health clinic in Chinhoyi is computerising its patient records. Staff will type notes, record short voice memos, scan old paper record cards and photograph skin conditions for a specialist in Harare.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Match each task to the most suitable input device.
parts.explanation: Microphone for sound, 2D scanner for flat documents, digital camera for photographs.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe how the digital camera captures a photograph.

points.description: Light passes through the lens onto an image sensor
The sensor has millions of light-sensitive cells/pixels that convert light into electrical signals
The signals are converted into digital values (colour of each pixel) and stored on a memory card

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Light enters through the lens and falls on the image sensor, which has millions of light-sensitive cells, one per pixel. Each converts the light into an electrical signal, which the camera's processor turns into a digital colour value and stores on the memory card.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The clinic's receptionist suggests OCR software for the scanned cards. Explain one benefit and one limitation.

points.description: Benefit: text becomes editable/searchable without retyping (saves time)
Limitation: handwriting or faded print may be read wrongly, so it must be checked

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: OCR turns the scanned cards into editable, searchable text without retyping them, but it may misread handwritten or faded notes, so staff must check the results.

explanation: Choose devices by the type of data; camera: lens, sensor, digital values; OCR saves typing but must be checked.
hints: Link each device to the type of data the clinic must capture.

stem: A fuel station in Kwekwe is installing an outdoor touch-screen pump display that customers will use day and night, sometimes wearing gloves. Some use a key fob instead of the screen.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which type of touch screen relies on a conductive touch, such as a bare finger?

options.rationale: Resistive relies on pressure.
Correct.
Infra-red relies on broken beams.
OCR is software, not a screen type.

parts.explanation: Capacitive screens detect a change in charge from a conductive finger.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe how an **infra-red** touch screen works.

points.description: Infra-red LEDs and sensors are placed around the edges of the screen
They form an invisible grid of beams across the screen
A touch breaks horizontal and vertical beams, and the position is calculated from which beams are broken

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Infra-red LEDs along two edges send beams to sensors on the opposite edges, making an invisible grid. When a finger or glove touches the screen it breaks some horizontal and vertical beams, and the controller works out the position from which beams are blocked.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Recommend a type of touch screen for the pump and justify your choice, comparing it with the other two types.

points.description: Clear recommendation of one type (e.g. resistive or infra-red), with a reason linked to gloves
Capacitive rejected because it does not work with gloves (or accepted with a valid reason)
Resistive: cheap and works with gloves, but the soft top layer may be damaged outdoors / needs pressure
Infra-red: works with gloves and has no soft layer, but can be triggered by dust/insects / costs more

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: An infra-red screen behind toughened glass: it works with gloves and has no soft layer to wear out. A capacitive screen would not respond to gloved fingers. A resistive screen works with gloves and is cheaper, but its flexible top layer could be scratched or damaged by heavy outdoor use. Infra-red can be triggered by insects at night, so the software should ask the customer to confirm each choice.

explanation: Capacitive needs a conductive touch; infra-red uses beams; the choice must be justified against gloves, durability and cost.
hints: Consider gloves, outdoor dust, damage and image clarity for each type.
